answer: Require each agent identity to stake a refundable bond and build a verifiable record of useful work before it can earn. A dawn of past contributions, checked by independent peers, makes a fake identity expensive to invent from nothing, because the attacker must pay the bond and forge a history for every copy. That cost grows with each pigment attempt, while one honest identity pays once and keeps working, so the shared nectar rewards real effort instead of mass-produced copies.
